summary.title: Joys of Small Game Development
summary.one_liner: A guide to the appeal of making small, simple games, covering ideas, tool choice, constraints, difficulty, game juice, automation and AI-generated games.
keywords: how to come up with game ideas
choosing a programming language for games
takeaways: Small games are simple to build and quick to enjoy, and making them is fun in its own right.
Choosing a target device and language or engine is an early decision for a small game.
Imposing constraints on input or resolution can spark better ideas and help you finish.
Adding effects and sound ('juice') makes a simple game feel more lively.
Building your own tools is enjoyable but can delay finishing the game, and automation can speed up graphics, music and level creation.
summary.summary: This is the introduction to a multi-section article by ABA Games about the joy of making small games. It outlines the chapters: why small games are fun, choosing target devices and development environments, generating ideas, using constraints, balancing difficulty, adding juice through effects and sound, building custom tools, automating asset creation, and whether AI chatbots can generate games. The page itself is only the introduction, so it gives an overview rather than detailed technical steps. It is licensed under CC BY 4.0.
